question: What was the share of industry in India's GDP in 1950-1951?
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.13**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
 

• In **1950-51**, the share of the industry in India’s **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** was approximately **13%**. This was a modest contribution due to India’s largely agrarian economy during the post-independence era. 

• At the time, the industrial sector was primarily focused on basic industries such as **textiles, food processing, and small-scale manufacturing**. Heavy industries were still in their nascent stages. 

• The economy of India was characterized by its reliance on agriculture, which accounted for the largest share of GDP, with industry and services contributing lesser proportions. 

• The **Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948** laid the foundation for industrial development in India, encouraging public and private sector participation in the economy. 

• Post-independence, India adopted a strategy of **state-led industrialization**, with emphasis on establishing public sector enterprises to build heavy industries and infrastructure.
